key_insight: Photoluminescence imaging combined with Bayesian inference can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade—at the electron or hole transport interfaces or in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This gives device engineers a practical way to diagnose failure modes spatially and to target passivation or interface design for longer-lived perovskite modules.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to experimental observations
Bayesian inference to estimate spatial maps of recombination-related parameters
evidence_signal: The inferred parameter maps were tracked during aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight, revealing strong spatial heterogeneity and identifying the most severe degradation at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The approach depends on model fidelity and image quality, so incorrect drift-diffusion assumptions or limited spatial resolution could bias the inferred degradation maps.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
